content:
Federico Viticci's annual iOS roundup is always a must-read at MacStories, and this year is no exception.

Federico writes that while iOS 27 isn't as flashy as last year's release, the update shows Apple is "still capable of bringing new things while taking care of old features."

I value Federico's take on AI, so I was particularly interested to read his thoughts on Apple Intelligence and Siri AI in iOS 27. Here's a small excerpt:

The new Siri is not an agentic product that can carry out lengthy tasks on its own, and comparing Siri AI to things like ChatGPT Work, Claude Cowork, Grok Bot, Hermes Agent, or OpenClaw is frankly absurd. I'd love for Siri AI to become that kind of experience in the future, and Apple seems to think it's laid the groundwork for agentic behavior one day. But as things stand, given that I rely on Notion, Slack, and Superhuman to get work done, and given how Siri AI is simple and not very smart, I can't imagine using Apple's assistant for productivity work. Instead, I've started to appreciate Siri AI for what it is — a better, smarter Siri whose goal isn't to replace your favorite agents for the time being — and I'm not disappointed that it can't do more yet. I enjoy using Siri with Apple Notes, Reminders, HomeKit, and third-party apps like AskPlay, Monologue, Alyx, MusicBox, and LookUp. What I've found Siri AI is best at is quick, one-off interactions, perhaps with one or two follow-ups, but it doesn't handle longer conversations. When I find I need deeper research with more turns, I switch to ChatGPT or Open Minis on iOS.
